task.description:
Hard gate on CODE-DESIGNER's design at lib/letflow/design/iss0451-poller-crash-budget-isolation.md. Independently re-derive your verdict from the artefact itself, not from CODE-DESIGNER's own result.summary (which you should treat as a claim to verify, not a fact to copy) -- see core-directives.md's 'Every producing step has a validating step'. Check specifically:
1. Does the design cover every one of ISS-0451's three acceptance criteria (docs/issues/ISS-0451.yaml): AC1 (a persistent-fault test scenario proving Letflow.Supervisor/Repo/Bandit survive), AC2 (documented restart-intensity arithmetic showing the fix tolerates at least one full Pollers-budget-exhaustion cycle), AC3 (no regression to REQ-219's own AC2 boot-order or AC4 single-crash-isolation tests)?
2. Is the arithmetic in the design actually correct? Work it through yourself rather than trusting the doc's own numbers -- re-derive independently whether the chosen top-level restart-intensity value plus the circuit-breaker's trip threshold genuinely prevents an indefinite persistent fault from ever exhausting the top-level supervisor's budget (not merely delaying it by a bounded, finite number of extra cycles).
3. Does the design contain any implementation code (.ex function bodies)? If it names a new module (e.g. a PollersBreaker GenServer), it should specify signatures/@specs/state-shape/callback contracts only -- fail this check if you find an actual function body implementing logic, not just a signature.
4. Is the design unambiguous enough for ELIXIR-DEV to implement without having to invent any missing decision (exact config keys, exact state machine transitions, exact backoff schedule values, exact module/file placement)?
5. Does the design explicitly state how REQ-219's own AC2 (boot order: Infrastructure before Pollers) and AC4 (single Pollers-budget-exhaustion event still leaves Infrastructure/Http alone) are preserved, with reasoning you can independently verify against the current code (lib/letflow/application.ex, lib/letflow/supervisor/pollers.ex)?
6. Is the specified regression-test mechanism (how the test keeps the fault persistent, unlike REQ-219's own AC4 test which clears it) concrete enough for TEST-DESIGNER to build without design ambiguity?

This is a hard gate -- FAIL with specific, itemized gaps (per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md's validator-fail worked example) if any check above doesn't pass; do not rubber-stamp.
acceptance_criteria: Verdict states explicitly, per ISS-0451 AC, whether AC1/AC2/AC3 are each covered by the design
Verdict states the validator's own independently re-derived arithmetic check result, not a repetition of CODE-DESIGNER's numbers
Verdict states explicitly whether any implementation code was found in the design doc
Verdict states explicitly whether REQ-219 AC2/AC4 preservation reasoning is checked and correct
A FAIL verdict lists every gap by section/line with what must change; a PASS verdict states what was independently re-derived and how

result.summary:
Read lib/letflow/design/iss0451-poller-crash-budget-isolation.md directly in full (698 lines), plus docs/issues/ISS-0451.yaml, the ISSUE-FIXER diagnosis handoff, lib/letflow/application.ex, lib/letflow/supervisor/pollers.ex, req219-supervision-layering.md, and test/letflow/supervisor/pollers_test.exs. AC1 (persistent-fault test proving Letflow.Supervisor/Repo/Bandit survive) is covered: §6 specifies a new test/letflow/supervisor/pollers_breaker_test.exs with a concrete procedure (§6.2) that never clears force_poller_crash mid-test and asserts Repo/Infrastructure/Http/top-level-Supervisor pids and a :DOWN-monitor refutation while the fault is still live. AC2 (documented restart-intensity arithmetic) is covered on its face: §1/§3.6/§4 state concrete numbers (breaker trip after 2 consecutive :DOWN events, top-level max_restarts raised 3->5). AC3 (no regression to REQ-219 AC2/AC4) is covered: §5 gives an explicit, checkable argument for both, and independently checking it against lib/letflow/application.ex and lib/letflow/supervisor/pollers.ex, the reasoning holds (children list order Infrastructure->Pollers->PollersBreaker->Http preserves AC2's boot-order guarantee; the breaker's two-consecutive-:DOWN threshold, cross-checked against pollers_test.exs's own AC4 test which clears the fault after exactly one :DOWN, means the breaker never leaves :closed during that existing test, so AC4 is unaffected). No implementation code found (grepped for def/defp/case-do patterns across the whole file: zero matches) -- the doc is signatures, state shapes, and prose throughout, consistent with req219-supervision-layering.md's precedent.

INDEPENDENTLY RE-DERIVED ARITHMETIC CHECK RESULT: FAILS. I re-derived, rather than trusted, whether the breaker's intervention genuinely bounds top-level restart consumption at 2 (the number §4's whole margin calculation, '5 - 2 = 3', depends on). The design's own mechanism (§3.4): the breaker's handle_info({:DOWN,...}) callback fires only when its OWN Process.monitor delivers a :DOWN message to its mailbox -- a message-passing hop distinct from, and not synchronized with, the top-level Supervisor's own internal automatic-restart-on-EXIT behavior, which reacts to the SAME child exit directly as part of Supervisor's own exit-trapping, with no extra message hop. So for the 2nd Pollers exit (the one that is supposed to trip the breaker): the top-level Supervisor's own automatic 3rd restart of Pollers is racing against the sequence 'monitor :DOWN delivered to PollersBreaker's mailbox -> handle_info scheduled and run -> Supervisor.terminate_child/2 call (itself a synchronous GenServer-call-shaped round trip) sent and completed'. Nothing in the BEEM scheduling model or in anything OTP's Supervisor/GenServer documented contracts guarantee the second, longer chain completes before the first, structurally shorter one. The design asserts the opposite at lines 414-417 ('no 3rd automatic restart is ever attempted, because terminate_child removes Pollers... before that budget could be threatened a 2nd time') and at line 333-335 ('so the top level does not even attempt a further automatic restart') -- but this is stated as a conclusion, not demonstrated, and §3.4's own line 326-328 punts the actual race analysis to 'see §3.6 for the exact race and why it is safe.' §3.6 (lines 375-424), read in full, never actually analyzes this race -- it analyzes a DIFFERENT race (single-shot vs. persistent fault, i.e. whether a 2nd :DOWN arrives before the observation timer elapses) and simply restates the same unproven claim ('no 3rd automatic restart is ever attempted') as if it were the resolution. §3.7 (lines 425-445) also assumes the claim rather than proving it ('rather than passively waiting for the top level to attempt and fail a 3rd automatic restart' -- presented as the alternative NOT taken, not as a race that could still happen anyway). Given ordinary BEAM message-passing latency, the top-level Supervisor's in-process reaction to the child's own EXIT is very likely faster than the breaker's monitor-message-then-GenServer-call chain, meaning a 3rd automatic top-level restart is plausible on every trip, not merely a theoretical edge case. This breaks §4's arithmetic directly: '5 (new ceiling) - 2 (breaker's own worst-case consumption) = 3' assumes worst-case consumption is 2; if it is actually 3 (or worse, if the 3rd auto-restarted Pollers instance also has time to begin a 3rd exhaustion cycle before terminate_child lands, re-arming rather than stopping the loop), the stated margin and the claim that the design 'tolerates at least one full Pollers-budget-exhaustion cycle' (AC2's own bar) are not established by this document as written. This is exactly the kind of concrete, checkable arithmetic gap ISS-0451's AC2 exists to force onto paper, and it is unresolved.

IMPLEMENTATION CODE CHECK: none found. No .ex/.exs function bodies present anywhere in the document -- confirmed by full-file review and a def/defp/case-do grep returning zero matches. This check PASSES.

REQ-219 AC2/AC4 PRESERVATION CHECK: checked and correct as far as it goes (see AC3 paragraph above) -- but this verdict is independent of, and does not rescue, the arithmetic failure: AC3's reasoning in §5 explicitly leans on the same two-consecutive-:DOWN mechanism whose race-safety is unproven, so while REQ-219's EXISTING tests are correctly shown to be unaffected (the design's own two-:DOWN threshold genuinely does exceed the one :DOWN either existing test produces, independent of the race question), the NEW behavior ISS-0451 itself requires (bounding a persistent fault) is not yet demonstrated safe.

Overall: 2 of 6 task checks fail (checks 2 and, derivatively, 4's 'unambiguous enough for ELIXIR-DEV to implement without inventing a missing decision' bar, since resolving this race requires a decision -- e.g. synchronous terminate_child from inside the :DOWN handler before any other work, or setting Pollers' child spec to restart: :temporary so the top-level Supervisor never auto-restarts it at all and the breaker becomes solely responsible for restart_child calls -- that this design does not make). Per WF-02 Step 1b's 'FAIL immediately on any check failure -- no partial credit' and per this project's hard-gate convention, this is a FAIL, not a PARTIAL.

issues.description: lib/letflow/design/iss0451-poller-crash-budget-isolation.md §3.4/§3.6/§3.7/§4: the design claims (lines 333-335, 414-417, 425-445) that PollersBreaker's terminate_child call after the 2nd :DOWN prevents any 3rd automatic top-level restart of Pollers, and sizes §4's top-level intensity margin (5 - 2 = 3) on that claim. This is asserted, not demonstrated. The top-level Letflow.Supervisor's own automatic restart-on-exit reacts directly to the child's EXIT signal (no extra message hop); PollersBreaker's intervention requires its own Process.monitor :DOWN message to be delivered to its mailbox, handle_info to be scheduled and run, and then a Supervisor.terminate_child/2 call (a synchronous round trip) to complete -- a strictly longer chain reacting to the SAME exit event, with no stated synchronization or ordering guarantee that it wins the race. §3.4 line 328 explicitly defers this exact race to '§3.6 for the exact race and why it is safe,' but §3.6 (lines 375-424) analyzes a different race (single-shot vs. persistent fault timing against the observation timer) and never addresses whether the top-level Supervisor's own restart can complete before terminate_child arrives. What must change: either (a) add an explicit mechanism that makes the top-level Supervisor structurally unable to auto-restart Pollers after the 2nd exit -- e.g. specify Pollers' child spec with restart: :temporary in Letflow.Application's children list, making PollersBreaker solely responsible for all restarts of Pollers via explicit restart_child calls, removing the race entirely -- or (b) provide an actual proof/citation that OTP's Supervisor guarantees the monitor-and-terminate_child path completes before the Supervisor's own internal restart for the same exit (if such a guarantee exists, cite the exact OTP contract; a bare assertion is insufficient for AC2's own 'documented restart-intensity arithmetic' bar), and (c) re-derive §4's margin arithmetic under whichever real worst-case consumption count applies (which may be 3, or higher if a 3rd auto-restarted Pollers instance has time to begin its own exhaustion cycle before termination lands).

result.next_action: Rework CODE-DESIGNER -- 1 BLOCKER above (race-condition gap in the breaker's termination-vs-automatic-restart ordering, undermining AC2's arithmetic), rework iteration 1 of 3. Route back to CODE-DESIGNER, not ELIXIR-DEV; do not advance to Step 2a.
